selector.rationale: Ovarian cancer best explains the findings of bilateral pleural and pericardial effusions, lytic bone lesions, and elevated CA-125, despite the ultrasound not showing ovarian masses, which could be due to the cancer being at an early stage or not visibly detectable by ultrasound.

rejected.label: Meigs syndrome
rejected.why: Lack of strong evidence and presence of lytic bone lesions not typical for Meigs syndrome

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Insufficient evidence to support this diagnosis given the presence of lytic bone lesions and elevated CA-125

rejected.label: Pericardial Effusion due to Malignancy
rejected.why: While this could be a part of the presentation, it is less specific than ovarian cancer which explains more findings
